title: A polar section on a proper valuation curve with one rational component
statement: Let $K$ be a separably closed [def-kun-separably-closed] field [def-weil-field] and $V\subset K$ a valuation ring with fraction field $K$: for every $a\in K^\times$, either $a$ or $a^{-1}$ lies in $V$. Assume that the prime ideals of $V$ form a finite chain, and put $T=\operatorname{Spec}V$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum], with generic point $\eta=\operatorname{Spec}K$. Let $Y$ be a normal proper $T$-curve with geometrically reduced fibres, and let $s$ be the closed point of $T$. Suppose $Z\subset Y_s$ is an irreducible component geometrically isomorphic to a projective line [def-nagata-projective-space-base-change]. Then $Z\simeq\mathbf P^1_{\kappa(s)}$. Assume that $Y_s$ is nodal along $Z$, and that the intersection of $Z$ with the union of the other components consists of at most two transverse branches. No semistability of $Y$ away from $Z$ is assumed. Write $Z_1,\ldots,Z_n$ for the other irreducible components of $Y_s$ [def-weil-irreducible-components]. There are pairwise disjoint horizontal effective Cartier divisors $P_i\subset Y$ in the relative smooth locus [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms], each isomorphic to $T$, such that $(P_i)_s$ is a smooth $\kappa(s)$-rational point $p_i$ of $Z_i$ outside every other component and outside $Z$. For some integer $m>0$, put $P=m\sum_i P_i$ and $L=\mathcal O_Y(P)$ [def-pc-divisor-line-bundle, def-sc-invertible-module]. There exists $a\in\Gamma(Y,L)$ whose value in the one-dimensional fibre $L\otimes\kappa(p_i)$ is nonzero for every $i$. The divisors are effective Cartier in the sense that their ideals are locally generated by one non-zero-divisor; $\mathcal O_Y(P)$ is the dual of that ideal. In a local parameter cutting out $P_i$, the meromorphic function represented by $a$ has pole of order exactly $m$ on the closed fibre at $p_i$ and no poles outside $P$. The canonical section $e=1\in\Gamma(Y,L)$ has zero divisor $P$. The same assertion permits $n=0$, with $P=0$. A $T$-curve means a flat [def-weil-flat-morphism] finitely presented [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] $T$-scheme of pure relative dimension one [def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. A geometric fibre is the base change of a fibre to an algebraic closure of its residue field [def-weil-geometric-fibre]; geometrically reduced means all such fibres have no nonzero nilpotents. An $\eta$-modification is a proper morphism [def-weil-proper-morphism] which is an isomorphism over the generic fibre and over schematically dense open subschemes; schematic density means injectivity of $\mathcal O_Z\to j_*\mathcal O_U$ for the open inclusion. A scheme is normal if every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Its normalization means the scheme obtained by taking the integral closure of its structure sheaf in the product of the function fields of its irreducible components; for an integral scheme this is [def-sc-normalization]. Nodal along $Z$ means that after algebraic closure of the residue field each singularity there has completed local ring $\Omega[[u,v]]/(uv)$ [def-weil-pbc-adic-completion, def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series].
